entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: %s over a subquery wrapping a native-histogram-valued shape is unsupported
entries.rationale: unreachable since cerberus issue #2724: outer.Func.Name reaching this point already passed the chplan.IsPromQLRangeWindowFunc(canonicalRangeWindowFunc(...)) guard above, so it is one of that vocabulary's 26 names. lowerHistogramOrMixedSubqueryOuterFnInput (histogram_native_mixed_or_subquery_further_setop_range_fn.go) matches every one of the fifteen SELECT/FOLD-family names unconditionally (its own switch has no default-false case for any of them, only for names outside that set) and returns before this line whenever it matches. The other eleven names IsPromQLRangeWindowFunc admits are exactly histogramSubqueryFloatOnlyDropFunc's own set, which the very next branch below already handles instead of falling through here. Every name in the 26-name vocabulary is therefore claimed by one of those two branches, and this return can never execute. Before #2724, only histogramSubqueryFloatOnlyDropFunc's eleven names and a narrow, AST-recognizer-gated slice of the fifteen SELECT/FOLD names composed here, leaving this a real, reachable divergence (tracking issues #2581, then #2615, then #2724 as each closed leaf narrowed what remained) — #2724's own shape-dispatch, not AST recognition, is what makes the fifteen-name coverage total rather than partial.

guard: if shape := chplan.RowShapeOf(inner); shape == chplan.HistogramRowShape || shape == chplan.MixedRowShape
past returning if node, matched, err := lowerHistogramOrMixedSubqueryOuterFnInput(inner, shape, outer.Func.Name, sub, s, ctx); matched

entries.head: promql
entries.message: promql: %s does not accept a subquery argument
entries.rationale: unreachable: a PromQL function that takes a range-vector argument is either a member of the shared range-window vocabulary (chplan.IsPromQLRangeWindowFunc, consulted through canonicalRangeWindowFunc so the double_exponential_smoothing source spelling resolves to its IR name) or absent_over_time, and the arm directly above this guard routes absent_over_time to lowerAbsentOverTimeOverSubquery, so no parseable query reaches it
